required_fixes: Overlap operationalization does not realize prereg definition: prereg requires 0/25/50/75/100% as proportion of noise distribution overlapping failure region. Code implements shift = overlap_pct/100 * 0.09 (mock_server.py:_draw_session_quality). Actual theoretical overlap is 0% at 25%, 0% at 50% (per code [0.095,0.185] vs failure [0.20,0.39]), ~8% at 75% ([0.1175,0.2075]) and ~33% at 100% ([0.14,0.23]). Even report table [0.11,0.20]/[0.14,0.23]/[0.17,0.26]/[0.20,0.29] (0%/30%/60%/100%) misstates code. A genuine 25%/50% overlap test was never executed — FP=0 at 25%/50% is not evidence against discrimination, it is artifact of insufficient shift. Redesign with failure distribution shift downward or larger noise range or Gaussian overlap to achieve true 25%/50% area overlap.

Threshold calibration grid is coarse discrete [0.20,0.25,...0.80] with tie-break lowest-threshold-wins. With FP=0 at all thresholds for 0-50% (noise max <0.20 per design), argmax-F1 trivially selects lowest threshold regardless of underlying continuous optimum. Calibrated threshold constancy 0.20 at 0-75% does not demonstrate absence of gradual shift — the optimum between 0.20-0.25 was not probed. Future design must use continuous threshold sweep or ROC analysis to locate discriminating point.

Orthogonality marginal failure at 75% (r=0.066326, CI upper 0.154909 >0.15, C3_pass false while TOST p_upper=0.032 passes) is dismissed as sample-size artifact in report.md without power calculation. At n=480 SE=0.045787, delta=0.15 requires |r| <0.06 to pass CI<delta. Observed r=0.066 just exceeds margin and may indicate genuine correlation emergence when noise enters failure zone (75% is first condition with nonzero FP). Requires n>=800 or replicated measurement before attributing to noise.

Mock-only ceiling remains: all signals via /api/session/status session_quality uniform draws on localhost Flask 3.1.3 + SQLite WAL + JWT + jitter 10-100ms. No production OAuth/OIDC, CDN, network RTT, DB-backed sessions. Parent handoff next_question about production-like substrate with FP>0 at calibrated threshold remains open. No inference to production refresh quality distributions which likely are not uniform.

Positive/negative control labeling in result.json::controls is contradictory: NC-FP-BINDING-25 and NC-FP-BINDING-50 expect FP>0 (positive expectation) but are labeled NC, and PC-FP-BINDING-75/100 are labeled PC. This does not invalidate measurements but obscures control semantics and decision-rule evaluation. Align control IDs to falsifiable expectations (e.g., PC binds at high overlap, NC null at 0%).

claim_ceiling: C-FRESHNESS remains EXPERIMENTAL, mock-only. Narrowly established: on localhost Flask 3.1.3 + SQLite WAL + JWT HS256/RS256 with synthetic uniform session_quality, calibrated threshold 0.20 survives label overlap up to 75% (actual overlap ~8%, FP=0.0958 <0.10) and only shifts to 0.25 at 100% label shift (actual overlap ~33%, FP=0.35 violates constraint). Threshold response is flat at 0.20 for 0-75% then single jump to 0.25 — not the hypothesized gradual increase — and FP binding fails for 25%/50% because design produced 0% actual overlap. Orthogonality TOST delta=0.15 holds at 4/5 label overlaps (r -0.004 to 0.036) but marginally fails at 75% (r=0.066 CI upper 0.1549 >0.15) where FP first emerges. Discrimination 0.8333 and 4/4 noise types remain effective. No evidence for production OAuth/OIDC, CDN, network RTT, DB sessions, or non-uniform production refresh distributions. Do not promote to PRODUCT_CORE or VALIDATED; do not assume threshold 0.20 is discriminating under production overlapping noise.
unresolved: Why does FP binding fail at 25%/50% label overlap despite intended design? Audit finds code shift too small to create actual distributional overlap — is a corrected design (larger shift, Gaussian, or failure mean shift) sufficient to produce FP>0 at 25%/50% with gradual threshold increase, or is guard genuinely robust to moderate overlap?

Is non-monotonic flat-then-jump threshold response (0.20 across 0-75% then 0.25 at 100%) a property of uniform shift design/0.05 discrete grid or genuine freshness guard characteristic? Continuous threshold ROC not tested.

Does marginal orthogonality failure at 75% (CI upper 0.1549 vs delta 0.15) replicate with n>=800 or is it sampling variation? 75% is only condition where FP first emerges, suggesting possible induced behavioral-structural correlation under partial overlap.
Would Gaussian or production-like noise distributions with gradual tails produce earlier FP binding and different FP-TP tradeoff than uniform shifted box?
How does calibrated threshold behave at intermediate label overlaps (e.g., 10,30,60,80,90%) under corrected overlap definition?

Does threshold increase and orthogonality pattern persist on production-like substrate with real OAuth/OIDC, CDN, network RTT, DB-backed sessions where noise/refresh distributions may be correlated, as per request.json inherited_next_question?
